newsitem.title: USA: Healthdyne says receives acquisition offers. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Healthdyne says receives acquisition offers. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]

text.p: Healthdyne Technologies Inc., the maker of medical equipment that is battling a $200 million takeover bid by Invacare Corp., said Wednesday other possible buyers have expressed interest in the company.
Healthdyne said one of the possible buyers is an unidentified company listed on the Fortune 500 that is willing to pay more than Invacare's current bid of $15 a share.

The announcement from Healthdyne came one week before the company's annual meeting of shareholders, at which Invacare is seeking to oust some of Healthdyne's directors in an attempt to complete its proposed takeover.
Invacare, based in Elyria, Ohio, had no immediate comment on Healthdyne's announcement.
Healthdyne Chairman Parker H. Petit said, "We believe we can achieve higher value for shareholders after the board is re-elected."
Healthdyne, which previously had said the company was not for sale, last month said it would talk with interested parties about a potential transaction.
Healthdyne did not identify any of the potental buyers. Nor did it say if any of them have made a bid. It said the Fortune 500 company "has a strong strategic interest" in acquiring Healthdyne.

The company also said that its board, if re-elected at the July 30 annual meeting, will amend the company's bylaws to permit holders of at least 25 percent of the company's common stock to call special shareholder meetings, and amend its shareholder rights plans to allow a bidder, who meets certain conditions, to call a special meeting of shareholders to vote on a binding resolution to redeem the rights.

Healthdyne also said that, in the event that Invacare's four nominees were elected at the meeting, its board had authorised a $1.0 million trust to be used by the company's continuing directors to pay the expenses associated with any action taken by Invacare or its nominees.

These include an appeal by Invacare against a July 3 district court decision upholding a continuing directors provision of Healthdyne's shareholder rights plan, a provision Invacare was seeking to eliminate.
Healthdyne has rejected Invacare's $200 million hostile bid as inadequate.
In late morning trading, Healthdyne's stock was up 83 cents at $17.69 and Invacare was down 50 cents at $23.50, both on Nasdaq.
Healthdyne makes home health products for sleep disorders, breathing and infant monitors. It had sales of $118 million in 1996.
Invacare makes wheel chairs, medical care beds, respiratory products and cardiovacscular equipment and had sales of $610 million in 1996.
